doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Neighbors and the New England arts scene
summary: Living near Benny Goodman, John Hammond, Bernstein and the Cage circle.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: So think about what the east coast was like in those days, and who was there. We were about a half a mile from Benny Goodman’s house in Connecticut. We were — in urban terms say blocks, but the reality was that we were a large hayfield away from John Hammond’s house. Leonard Bernstein was, you know a drive away. He wasn’t that close but he wasn’t that far. John Hersey was around there someplace, the author. The next door neighbors included a painter whose reputation is kind of gone now, but Jean Jackson who was very close to Xenia Cage, John Cage’s wife, who was a frequent visitor, which meant that sometimes Virgil Thompson came up to the country to hang out and, you know, in a few words we had gone from an ambience in California where you know, little league baseball was kind of a good metaphor from where we were to where it was happening at the time.
Dave and Iola were just — acclimatized quickly and wonderfully to that.
